summary:
Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba) consists of three special municipalities within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Dutch national law governs civil status, marriage and anti-discrimination, and the same statutory framework that applies in the European Netherlands operates on the islands.

Same-sex unions have been registrable in the islands since 2012. On 4 December 2012 the Census Office in Saba registered the first such union in the Caribbean Netherlands, between Cedeno Xiomar Gonzalez, an Aruban national aged 26, and Israel Ernesto Ruiz Pinto, a Venezuelan national aged 27. Both were visiting residents rather than local inhabitants, establishing that the registry performs civil ceremonies for persons without island residency.

Practical arrangements for a civil ceremony are documented on Saba. Saba Tourism identifies the Court Room in the Administrative Building as the most straightforward venue for an efficient civil ceremony, and records registrar Julieta Woods as flexible in accommodating couples' requests. The island maintains a functioning destination-wedding infrastructure, including caterers, florists and accommodation providers.
tangentialFactors:
The 2012 union in Saba involved an Aruban national and a Venezuelan national, so couples arriving from outside the Dutch Caribbean face normal immigration and document requirements of their own origin countries regardless of the ceremony's legality in the territory.

Bonaire is promoted by travel media as an equality-friendly destination within the Caribbean region, and the islands operate on the US dollar, a detail relevant to couples arranging ceremonies or travel.

The Kingdom's civil-status framework covers all three islands in the same way, meaning the Saba registry precedent applies to Bonaire and Sint Eustatius as well, though the documented instances come from Saba.
localsOnly:
Residents of the Caribbean Netherlands enter civil status through the same island registry procedure documented on Saba, with the Census Office handling registration of unions and the registrar's role covering ceremony logistics as well as the paperwork itself.

Destination-wedding service providers operate on Saba for couples who want more than the registry ceremony alone, and the court room in the Administrative Building is the standard civil venue rather than a separate wedding office.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not state whether couples must register their intention in advance, what document requirements apply to non-resident couples, or whether an appointment is needed beyond contacting the registrar; these logistics are not sourced here.

No data in the inventory addresses enforcement of anti-discrimination protections on the islands, treatment of trans individuals specifically, or document and marker rules for identity papers — these remain unresolved for this record.
